title: How people discover new products: Lenny's seven channels and how to pick yours
summary: Lenny lays out seven ways people become aware of a new product, from friend referrals to outbound sales, with examples and the conditions under which each channel works. He closes with a five-step process for picking where to invest based on your early adopters.

principles.text: Friend-to-friend word of mouth is the cheapest, best growth channel, but only if the product is naturally suited to it.
principles.quote: This is by far the cheapest and best way to grow if you can pull it off.

principles.text: Invest in word of mouth only if the product is better with others, fun to share, or remarkable. You can't layer it on later.
principles.quote: Most products do not grow this way (and it’s nearly impossible to layer on if the product isn’t naturally suited for this), so don’t be sad if you can’t make this work.

principles.text: Organic discovery online works when your product is remarkable, people already search for it, or your company makes a good story.
principles.quote: Your product or company makes for a good story—one that reporters would want to cover, for example

principles.text: Paid online promotion fits products people don't search for, where new users generate revenue that funds more ads.
principles.quote: You generate revenue directly from new users (e.g., purchasing a product, subscribing to a service), which you can then use to fund more ads

principles.text: Outbound sales suits high AOV/LTV products, ones needing hand-holding, and early companies hunting their first customers.
principles.quote: That are just getting started and looking for their initial customers

principles.text: Pick channels by finding early adopters, where they spend time, then the quickest and cheapest way to reach them and what makes you stand out.
principles.quote: What’s the _cheapest_ way you can get in front of this group?
